newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt puts in strong performance at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt puts in strong performance at close.

text.p: New Zealand debt markets put in a solid performance on Tuesday to finish around seven points stronger across the curve.

Dealers said short bonds, buoyed by an overnight NZ$100 million February 2000 eurokiwi by borrower Toyota Motor Credit Corp, led the charge lower. A 10 billion yen dual currency samurai bond for Australia's Export Finance and Insurance Corp gave the market a further fillip.
The 02/00 bond ended six basis points stronger at 6.93 percent while its corresponding futures contract was seven points stronger at 93.03 on volume of 90 contracts.
Good buying was also seen in the longer bonds during the afternoon.

"The 02/00s in particular, as the low point on the yield curve, are the favoured stock for the dual currency and eurokiwi activity. You're also seeing the 11/06s mirror to a lesser or greater extent the international moves, particularly the U.S. 10-years, so you're getting driven down by one force and pushed up by the other," one Wellington bond dealer said.
Another dealer said the market was bullish ahead of Friday's key inflation data, with most traders going in long and expecting a good number.

"With the TWI up here and the RB's (Reserve Bank) assumed mix of conditions, we can see the rates lower than this. People are saying it's a one-way bet at the moment. If it (the inflation data) comes in bad, obviously they are going to be reassessing," she said.

The Reserve Bank is forecasting December quarter underlying inflation at 0.5 percent for an annual rise of 2.3 percent, while the market is more optimistic. A Reuters poll of economists showed an average expectation of a 0.4 percent quarterly rise, for an annual rise of 2.15 percent.
